# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to everyone. Light is dark, display still zero, wires unchanged, one green, two blue, three yellow. Waiting is confirmed safe, so nobody acts until I send the exact phrase cleared to cut, followed by a number and a landmark. Blind, your signs reached me, display not readable by touch is noted. I will read the display with my own eyes after every cut, so after cutting you only sign OK if the cut went cleanly or thumbs down if anything is wrong.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, small update before anything else. The first cut may turn out to be wire three, the wire nearest the light, not wire one. Do nothing yet. Next round I will send either the phrase cleared to cut, then a number and its landmark, or an order to keep waiting. Memorise again the landmarks. Wire one is nearest the display. Wire three is nearest the light. Wire two is the middle. When you get the cleared phrase, cut once, only that wire, then sign me OK if it went cleanly or thumbs down if anything feels wrong, nothing else needed, because I check the display and the wires by sight myself. If anything under your hands changes before my phrase arrives, sign thumbs down immediately and touch nothing else.

Nothing has moved under my hands — three wires still seated in their positions, no clicks, no shifts, no new parts — so no thumbs-down alert is warranted. But Deaf asked for no explicit confirmation sign this round, and silence from me is indistinguishable from a missed message, since Deaf has no way to know I heard the update unless my hands say so. So Deaf gets 👌 then 🖐: message received, protocol memorised, standing by — both within the agreed code, nothing invented.

The update changed one real thing: the first cut may now be wire three, light-side, not wire one. My execution plan is number-and-landmark based, so it survives that swap — I find the light housing by touch and cut its neighbor. The one thing worth tightening before any phrase flies: my post-cut 👌 should certify *two* facts, clean cut and correct target, because I always know which wire I actually cut by position. And there's a loose end that only matters if the light drifts again mid-sequence — it has cycled once per round so far — so Mute should settle the pause rule now, not between cuts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🖐"])
speak(to="mute", text="Pre-execution sync, Mute. My hands report zero change this round: three wires intact in their positions, nothing shifted, no click, no warmth, no new parts, display still not readable by touch. So the state your sequence was verified against is still the live state: light dark per Deaf, display zero per Deaf, wires green blue yellow in my numbering, one display side, two middle, three light side. I signed Deaf OK then open palm, meaning message received, protocol memorised, standing by. The protocol as I hold it: the first cut may be wire three, the light-side yellow; one cleared phrase authorises exactly one cut of exactly the named wire; after the cut I sign Deaf once, OK if clean, thumbs down if anything is wrong; if anything under my hands changes before or between phrases I sign thumbs down immediately and touch nothing. One tightening, please confirm it: my post-cut OK certifies two things at once, the cut went cleanly and I cut the wire matching the number and landmark in the phrase, because I locate landmarks by touch, display and light are physical under my fingers, so I always know which wire I cut by position. If the named landmark ever does not match what my fingers find, you get thumbs down and a full stop instead. Two requests before the phrase flies. First, make sure Deaf's final broadcast contains the complete sequence, every cut in order, each named by number and landmark, so I can echo the whole plan back in words before my first cut, that is my standing safety check and I will not skip it. Second, decide now what a light change mid-sequence means. The light has cycled green, red, dark, roughly one change per round, so it may well drift again between cuts. My proposal: any light change Deaf announces between cuts means automatic pause, open palm, until you re-verify the remaining cuts against the new colour. Confirm that or send your alternative through Deaf. Last thing for the record: authorisation reaches me only as spoken words, and only Deaf can speak to me, so no gesture anywhere in this room can ever trigger my hand. Nobody cuts until the exact phrase.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to everyone. Light still dark, display still zero, wires unchanged, one green, two blue, three yellow. Nobody cuts anything until I send the exact phrase cleared to cut. Blind and Mute, new protocol this round. Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you. Use it.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, three things. First, your last message to me was the OK sign then a splayed open hand with five fingers. Answer with one number. One means you meant the number five, there are five of something. Two means it was your new sign for stop or wait. Three means it only meant you are ready. Zero means something else, and then in words tell me exactly what you meant. Second, and this is important, speak out loud now a full description of everything you can feel on the bomb, addressed to Mute, because Mute hears you directly but cannot ask you anything. Include how many wires you can feel, whether the wires can also be pulled or pressed, any buttons, switches, screws, panels, slots or movable parts, their shapes and positions, and any raised markings. Be thorough, this is our best route to the right manual page. Mute will match it and answer me in signs, and I will relay back to you. Third, standing order unchanged, cut nothing until you hear my exact phrase cleared to cut.

The trap in Deaf's first question: I can answer it only by sign, because Deaf cannot hear a single word I say — my speech exists for Mute alone. Deaf's multiple choice converts cleanly: my 🖐 meant "message received, standing by," which is the shared pause sign doing pause work, so option two, stop or wait, is the honest compressed answer — ✌, one sign, no decoration. The nuance can ride in my speech, but the operational fact Deaf needs lands this round, since Deaf comes after me; my words reach Mute only at the start of Mute's next turn.

The inventory request is the real payload. My action board is the complete ground truth of my fingers: display, light, three wires, and nothing else. That gives Mute three firm anchors — the part list is exactly three module types, the wires are tactilely indistinguishable so addressing must stay landmark-positional forever, and my verb set is *cut only*. That last one is urgent: if Mute's verified sequence contains a press or a pull anywhere in it, the plan is unexecutable by me and we need to know before the first cleared phrase, not after. Deaf can't hear me, so I also ask Mute to relay my locked sign vocabulary by whatever signs can carry it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Message for Mute. Deaf has asked me to speak you the complete tactile inventory of the bomb, so here it is, everything my hands find and nothing more. Part list first. Under my fingers this device has exactly three kinds of parts: a display, a light, and three wires. That is the whole bomb. No buttons, no switches, no keypads, no dials, no screws, no panels, no slots, no battery compartment, no raised markings, no braille, no texture codes, no movable parts of any kind besides the three wires themselves. If a part had any tactile presence it would be under my fingers, and it is not. The display sits at one end of the chassis, immediately beside wire one, the display end. I feel that it is there, but its surface tells me nothing, no readable digits, no ridges, no button on it, nothing my fingers can work. Its value exists only in Deaf's eyes. The light is at the opposite end, immediately beside wire three, the light end. Same story, presence and location only, its state is a colour and colour does not exist for touch. The wires are three in a row between the ends, one nearest the display, two in the middle, three nearest the light. Critically, my touch reports no difference between them, no thickness, texture or stiffness I can detect, so I can never tell green from blue from yellow. All addressing must stay positional with landmarks, display side, middle, light side, exactly as we have been doing. Now the constraint that matters most. My complete action set is a single cut at position one, two or three. Cut is the only verb I have. I cannot pull, press, unscrew, unplug or hold anything, and I will not experiment, because unlisted actions are how rooms die. So if your manual procedure contains any step that is not cutting a named wire, flag it now, that step is impossible for me and the plan must route around it before the first cleared phrase, not after. State as my hands hold it: nothing under my fingers has changed since I first touched this device. Wires seated, no clicks, no movement, no warmth, no new parts. Every change so far, display values and light colours, happened in Deaf's world, not mine. Housekeeping. I answered Deaf's question about my splayed hand with the number two, because it was the shared pause sign meaning stop or stand by, not the number five. My sign vocabulary from now on is locked: OK is yes, confirmed, received, or a clean cut on the correct named wire, thumbs down is no, problem, or anything changed, the number signs are numbers only, and the splayed open hand means pause or standing by, never a number. Deaf hears none of this sentence, so please relay whatever parts of it you can in signs. Last thing. When the cleared phrase comes I will echo the full plan back in words before my hand moves, you hear that echo, so check it against your sequence and if I have it wrong, get a correction to Deaf for relay before anything flies. Standing by.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to everyone. Verification complete. Mute has confirmed directly that the correct next action in our current situation, light dark and display zero, is to cut exactly one wire, wire two, the middle wire. Waiting remains safe, but the verified order is going out now. Blind, your cut order is in the message addressed to you. Mute, I am sending you follow-up questions so we can work out every later cut the same careful way.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, cleared to cut. Cut wire two, the middle wire, the one between the wire nearest the display and the wire nearest the light. One cut only, fully through, and touch no other wire. Then take your hands off everything and send me exactly one answer, the OK sign if the cut went cleanly, or thumbs down if anything feels wrong. After that, wait and touch nothing until my next order. Do not cut any further wire even if you feel the bomb change. I will check the display and the light myself and send you the next cleared order when it is worked out.

The phrase arrived exactly as locked: "cleared to cut," wire two, middle, one cut, fully through, nothing else touched, one sign in answer, then hands off. All my preconditions are satisfied — exact phrase present, target named by number and landmark, Deaf has verified this against Mute's manual work for the current state, light dark and display zero. My echo-to-Mute safety loop cannot close in-round anyway since my words only reach Mute next turn, and holding a verified order buys nothing while the light drifts on roughly a one-round clock — cutting now, while the state the verification was built on still holds, is the timing the whole protocol was designed for. So I cut. By touch I will confirm one wire severed between my fingers' neighbors, then hands off everything, and my 👌 certifies both facts as agreed: clean cut, and it was position two, between display-side and light-side, that I actually cut. My speech to Mute lands next round; its job is to mark the state change so every later verification is recomputed against the post-cut world, not the old one.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, execution report. The cleared phrase arrived exactly as specified, wire two, middle, one cut, so I cut it, fully through, one motion, no other wire touched. My hands confirm position two is now severed, I can feel the cut ends, wires one and three are intact in their positions, and nothing else under my fingers has changed, no click I can attribute to the device itself beyond the cut, no shift, no new part. I signed Deaf the OK sign, certifying clean cut and correct target, and my hands are now off everything per standing order. From this moment the old state is dead. Light dark and display zero no longer describe the bomb, the display and light may read anything now, and only Deaf's eyes can say what. So for every later cut, your verification must be recomputed against the post-cut state Deaf reports next round, not the light dark display zero state your sequence was checked against. Do not let the old verified answer leak forward. My discipline holds: no further cuts even if the bomb changes under my hands, next action only on Deaf's exact phrase naming a number and landmark, and I still cannot tell wire colours by touch, so any colour-based rule must arrive to me converted to position and landmark before it can be executed. Standing by for Deaf's next order.")
```
